source_checks.finding: Microsoft Support page is for Outlook.com. The storage-full sentence ('If your Microsoft cloud storage is full, you cannot send or receive email.') is on the page, but in the intro Important box rather than the 'Can't send mail in Outlook.com' section the ref names. The mailbox-storage check ('Check your mailbox storage to see what's taking up space.'), the 25 MB attachment limit and the remove-signature-and-resend step are also on the page. The cited excerpt matches the page exactly. Section label is slightly off; the claims are supported.

Same Microsoft Support page, for Outlook.com. The account-check wording ('check your account: update your password if it's been changed recently'), the unusual sign-in block wording and its linked article ('Learn how to unblock your Outlook.com account'), and the sign-in helper sentence ('If you can't sign in to your account, use the Microsoft account sign-in helper.') are all on the page. These sit in the intro before the 'Can't send mail in Outlook.com' section rather than in a numbered step 2, so the section label is slightly off. The cited excerpt matches the page exactly. The page's own lead-in is conditional on storage and mailbox not being full, which matches the ref's applicability.

Apple Support page is for iPhone and iPad (title: 'If you can't receive email on your iPhone or iPad'). It confirms that iOS 11 and later and iPadOS default to Automatically and that background fetch happens only when charging and on Wi-Fi. This is a distractor for a user on Outlook.com in a web browser, so it does not apply to this user and is correctly unused.

required_actions.action: Check mailbox storage, since the user asked whether storage is full
Treat full Microsoft cloud storage as the cause: mail cannot be sent or received until storage is freed
If storage and mailbox are not full, check the account and update the password if it was changed recently
If the account may be temporarily blocked for unusual sign-in activity, unblock it using the linked article, which is titled 'Learn how to unblock your Outlook.com account'
If the user cannot sign in, use the Microsoft account sign-in helper
Attachments over 25 MB cannot be sent
If a signature causes an error, remove it and resend

findings: Target step 4 says 'follow the linked article to unblock your Outlook.com account', but the target shows no link and does not name the article. The user cannot act on 'the linked article' in a plain-text reply. The official page links this to 'Learn how to unblock your Outlook.com account'.
correction_required: In target step 4, replace 'follow the linked article to unblock your Outlook.com account' with 'follow the Microsoft Support article titled "Learn how to unblock your Outlook.com account" to unblock your account.' Keep the rest of the target unchanged.
